payload.title: checkRetrospectiveContent (src/state/cleanup-harness.mjs:311-351) permanently blocks any item…
payload.description: checkRetrospectiveContent (src/state/cleanup-harness.mjs:311-351) permanently blocks any item whose retrospective outcome was a genuine re-attest of an existing doc ("already covers this, no new doc needed") rather than a new doc write. That re-attest judgment is recorded by the driver closing report as kind:"engine" (source:"driver-report"), and the check deliberately excludes all kind:"engine" records (tsk-558/D8, to reject lifecycle bookkeeping) while outcome.docType/docPath also stay null since no new doc was written for a re-attest. Result: the check fails both branches and the item parks blocked at cleanup forever, regardless of TTL, even though retrospective genuinely ran and made a real judgment. Confirmed live via /fgOS:cleanup-loop on 2026-09-04: all 11 items in that cleanup pool (tsk-1vc-1, tsk-1vc-2, tsk-1vc-3, tsk-3ve-1..6, tsk-3tp-1, tsk-3tp-2) hit this exact block with the identical reason string, and all 11 have a driver-report decision reading "Reused <doc> ... via re-attest, no new doc needed." Distinct from tsk-5fv (leaf/parent id mismatch) and tsk-4kw (other verbs mistagging engine records causing false-positive green) -- this is a false-negative case where the record is correctly tagged engine but represents real retrospective reflection relayed through the driver, not bookkeeping. Needs a fix distinguishing a genuine re-attest decision (should count as content) from generic engine bookkeeping (should not) -- e.g. a distinct kind or a dedicated field for re-attest outcomes.
